sources.title: Address to the Nation Outlining a New Economic Policy
sources.publisher: Richard Nixon Presidential Library / Public Papers
sources.provenance_note: Primary contemporaneous presidential source. No independent E1 is admitted at this cutoff; this case intentionally remains partially hydrated.
claims: The United States suspended dollar convertibility into gold as part of the New Economic Policy.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Bulletin, October 1971
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; public after T0 cutoff.
claims: The Bulletin described suspension of convertibility and the ensuing move by major currencies away from prior intervention limits.

sources.title: Statement on the Economic Stabilization Act Amendments of 1971
sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project / Public Papers
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; retained as contextual confirmation but does not cure the T0 independence gap.
claims: Trading partners agreed to currency realignment and the dollar's gold price was to be changed; convertibility itself was not restored.

sources.title: Short-Term Energy Outlook, May 2008
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous official energy-market report before cutoff.
claims: Oil prices rose amid supply disruptions, strong emerging-market demand and a system operating near capacity.

sources.title: Oil Market Report, May 2008
sources.provenance_note: Independent international energy source; current archive hosts the contemporaneous May 2008 release.
claims: The May 2008 OMR reduced demand-growth expectations while still describing a tight oil-market backdrop.

sources.title: Short-Term Energy Outlook, December 2008
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; directly tests whether demand destruction overwhelmed physical scarcity.
claims: By December 2008 the global downturn had sharply weakened petroleum demand and oil prices.

sources.title: Federal Reserve announces extensive new measures to support the economy
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous policy source before end-of-day cutoff.
claims: The Federal Reserve expanded asset purchases and established multiple facilities to support market functioning and credit.

sources.title: Investment Update: Gold prices swing as markets sell off
sources.provenance_note: Independent contemporaneous market-structure source before cutoff.
claims: Gold volatility was linked to broad liquidation and dollar-liquidity needs; ETF flows remained positive year to date.

sources.title: Gold Demand Trends Q2 2020
claims: Record gold-ETF inflows and large policy liquidity injections supported investment demand and price performance.

sources.title: Gold Market Commentary, March 2021
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; helps discriminate real-rate/liquidity from a generic scarcity narrative.
claims: Gold weakened as U.S. rates rose; by end-March 2021 gold was materially below its August 2020 record.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Bulletin, December 1979
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous Federal Reserve publication before cutoff.
claims: The Federal Reserve linked rapid gold and silver price movements to discouragement about inflation control and described firm anti-inflation action.

sources.title: CPI Detailed Report, November 1979
sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics / FRASER
claims: Consumer-price inflation remained very high entering 1980.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Bulletin, December 1980
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; supports the real-rate reversal mechanism and expression/path settlement.
claims: The Bulletin reviewed soaring precious-metal prices, inflation fears, restrictive policy, and the subsequent macro-financial reversal during 1980.
